discovery: Time reversal and wavefront shaping of waves in complex, multiply scattering media

nominees.name: Mathias Fink
nominees.affiliation: Institut Langevin, ESPCI Paris - PSL, France

subfield: Optics and wave physics of complex media
motivation: For more than a century, multiple scattering was seen as the fundamental barrier to imaging and focusing waves through disordered matter. Mathias Fink's time-reversal mirrors showed that waves propagating through complex media can be refocused exactly, and that disorder can even improve resolution beyond the diffraction limit of the aperture. Vellekoop and Mosk (2007) brought this principle to optics, demonstrating that by shaping the incident wavefront, coherent light can be focused through opaque, strongly scattering layers, with enhancement set by the number of controlled modes. These discoveries turned scattering from noise into a resource and connected mesoscopic wave physics with practical control. They opened a whole field: transmission-matrix measurement, imaging through tissue and multimode fibres, open eigenchannels, deep-tissue neurophotonics, optical computing with random media, and high-dimensional quantum photonics. Their impact spans acoustics, medical ultrasound, seismology, telecommunications and optics.
